references.text: Eve saw that the tree was good to eat and a delight to the eyes—the same pattern of seeing, desiring, and taking that Achan followed.
The command against coveting your neighbor's property, which Achan broke by coveting the spoil from Jericho.
Silver and gold from idols were to be devoted to destruction for Israel, something Achan ignored.
Joshua's command that all silver, gold, and bronze should be dedicated to the Lord—that which Achan stole from.
The introduction of Achan's sin involving the devoted things.
The judgment against Achan where the stolen goods are mentioned again.
Judas took the money and hid his sin—a parallel to Achan's act of taking and hiding.
James' description of how desire leads to sin and death—the same progression as with Achan: see, desire, take.
Warning against the lust of the flesh and the lust of the eyes—the same temptations that caused Achan to fall.
